USS Enterprise, CV-6. The legendary Yorktown-class aircraft carrier nicknamed "Big E," she was the most-decorated ship of World War II, participating in nearly every major naval engagement in the Pacific and surviving damage that sank other ships. Her combat record made her the archetype of American naval power in the aircraft carrier age.

Enterprise was commissioned in 1938 and was one of the few American carriers in the Pacific on December 7, 1941, though she escaped Pearl Harbor damage by being at sea during the attack. She participated in every major Pacific carrier battle: the Coral Sea in May 1942, Midway in June 1942, the Eastern Solomons in August 1942, and Santa Cruz in October 1942. At Midway, her air group contributed significantly to the sinking of four Japanese fleet carriers, the battle that reversed the war's trajectory in the Pacific.

Enterprise survived multiple bomb and torpedo hits throughout the war, including at Santa Cruz where she suffered 70 casualties and massive damage but remained operational. She earned 20 battle stars, more than any other American warship, and launched nearly 40,000 combat sorties during her service. Decommissioned in 1947 and scrapped in 1960, she was denied the memorial status given to USS Arizona and USS Missouri, a decision many deemed unjust for her distinguished record. As the most battle-hardened American warship of the Pacific Theater, she had been there at Pearl Harbor despite the attack, and she fought across the entire Pacific War.
